regime_context: Detector shows a still-broad but narrowing eligible set (22 of 49 themes eligible), with AI Infrastructure leading on momentum but carrying a thin 12.5% breadth bar ('mixed' Hurst) — leadership without internal cohesion. The only validated edge is the absolute-trend gate (drawdown avoidance), and the rotation radar shows one-narrative=false with no confirmed handoff, so this is a trend-following, size-down regime, not a prediction regime. Track record direction accuracy (0.46) is effectively coin-flip, so conviction should be capped low.
emerging_watch: Watching Energy (Equal-Weight) vs US Energy Complex for a leadership handoff: if the equal-weight energy theme's score overtakes the cap-weighted complex while broadening above 0.65 breadth with a 'trend' Hurst tag, the leadership is rotating toward domestic distribution rather than mega-cap integrateds — retire the watch if the complex keeps a 0.3+ score lead through the next 10 sessions.

theses.subject: US Energy Complex
theses.thesis: US Energy Complex is the most coherent 'staying-power' candidate: it is rank 2 (eligible), has the second-highest durability_bar (0.62) among leaders, and notably the broadest positive breadth (0.636) in the top tier — meaning the trend is carried across many names, not a single mega-cap. The absolute-trend gate (the one validated risk-control leg) is satisfied. Crowding_z 0.93 is elevated but below the 1.61 flagged as crowded, so no size-down required. This is a durability-and-breadth tilt, not a momentum chaser.
theses.dissent: Energy breadth can collapse fast if oil mean-reverts or a geopolitical premium unwinds; the 'mixed' Hurst tag on the sector suggests the trend is not cleanly persistent, and an unscheduled-surprise share of 0.75 means headline-driven reversals are common.

falsifier.text: XLE loses its 50-day moving average while the energy_complex theme drops out of the top 5 ranks by durability before the check-by date

theses.subject: Cybersecurity
theses.thesis: Cybersecurity is the cleanest trend-health read in the eligible set: rank 3, highest durability_bar (0.75), a 'trend' Hurst tag, and solid breadth (0.6). The trend gate is satisfied. The crowding_z of 1.61 flags it as crowded, which per the guardrails is a size-DOWN caution, not a fade — so the lean stays overweight only in the sense of holding rather than adding aggressively. This is a pure staying-power hold.
evidence: crowded=true with crowding_z 1.61 — treat as size-down, not a sell
theses.dissent: Crowded positions in momentum leaders are prone to sharp air-pockets on any negative surprise; the elevated crowding_z means the first sign of a downside catalyst could trigger rapid de-grossing by systematic funds.

falsifier.text: CIBR gives back its last 60 days of relative gains and Cybersecurity's durability_bar prints below 0.5 at the check-by date

theses.subject: Robotics & Automation
theses.thesis: Robotics & Automation sits in the bottom half of the eligible set with a score of 0.61 but crucially carries a 'mean-revert' Hurst tag and a durability_bar (0.53) that offers no trend persistence edge. The only validated edge in the detector is trend-gate drawdown avoidance, and a mean-reverting tag signals the trend is not sustained — so the gate is not meaningfully in force. No trend-health reason to be overweight.
evidence: rank 14 of 49 — weak momentum in current regime
theses.dissent: Mean-revert tags can still deliver oversold bounces, and BOTZ contains diversified secular automation exposure that could re-rate on any industrial capex surprise; avoiding is a tactical call, not a structural bear case.

falsifier.text: BOTZ breaks above its 20-week high and Robotics & Automation's hurst_tag flips to 'trend' with durability_bar above 0.6 at the check-by date

macro_narrative.note: market-level macro/policy/geo narrative flow; coincident, not per-theme, never a trigger
